text:
andrea: FYI saw a weird uptick in schema validation rejections for function calls in eu-west around 09:20 UTC. ~3.2k rejects in 5m :grimacing:

samir: ugh. is that the strict fncall gate or the new validator sampling?

andrea: strict gate, looks like. samples show random extra fields in the tool response and also a few cases of array vs object. example log: ```ERROR validate_fncall: expected object, got array (tool: search_index, request_id: 9f3a...)```

bobby: are those coming from Hosted or Dedicated customers? could be a client SDK bug.

andrea: majority from Hosted. request metadata shows route_id=chat/generic and model_variant=rlhf-v2-quant.

elaine: does console surface these rejects anywhere? i tried the fncall dashboard but filter by 'validation' shows almost nothing (maybe sampling)

andrea: that's the issue — dashboard only shows sampled rejects, and sampling rate got bumped down for eu-west last week. so alerts didn't fire.

samir: who owns sampling policy? i thought telemetry -> infra, but UX flagged reduced visibility.

bobby: telemetry team sets global defaults, but eng-platform can override per-route. looks like the override for chat/generic didn't apply after the canary.

elaine: reminder: we rolled a permissive revert for soft-degrades last Friday. could be it touched the sampling map.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-21T08:45Z completed for permissive-revert v1.3 -> routing policy flag toggled.

samir: okay that explains timing. suggestion: add a console quick-filter for 'fncall validation rejects' that shows both sampled and unsampled counts (estimates + raw).

andrea: yes, and show the top offending routes + model variants. For immediate ops, can we bump sampling for validation rejects in eu-west to 100% for 30m?

bobby: we can, but that will spike telemetry ingestion. need an explicit ok from telemetry infra for 30m full-sample.

elaine: also need to check quotas — if a lot of rejects are retried by clients, we might end up charging customers or burning Dedicated slots. metric to watch: retry_attempts_per_request.

samir: good call. can we add a short-lived derived metric: validation_reject_ratio = rejects / total_fn_calls per route and surface as a colored pill on the route list?

andrea: agreed. makes debugging faster than drilling into traces.

bobby: implementation plan: 1) telemetry infra authorizes short-term full-sampling (30m), 2) eng-platform flips sampling override for eu-west route namespace, 3) console team adds a temporary quick-filter view + validation_reject_ratio pill, 4) infra runs quick audit for ingestion cost impact.

elaine: i can prototype a mockup for the console pill now. will push screenshot to #design in 15m.

samir: i'll ping telemetry infra (cc @telemetry-oncall) and request sampling window.

andrea: until then i've added a lightweight alert in Sentry for sudden >1% validation_reject_ratio per route. it will only notify on-call to avoid pager fatigue.

bobby: also curious if the model_variant selection is causing malformed outputs. can we temporarily route chat/generic traffic to rlhf-v2-quant-fallback which has stricter output shaping?

andrea: we can, but that may increase latency. set as a canary fallback for 10% traffic?

samir: agree with canary. make sure rollout uses the same route_id so billing attribution stays consistent.

deploy-bot: route-change: chat/generic -> variant-fallback canary (10%) queued (requested by samir).

elaine: mockup posted: https://redwood.internal/design/1867 — includes pill and quick-filter states (all/sampled/unsampled).

andrea: nice. one UX note: include a small explainer tooltip about sampling and how counts are estimated vs raw. I had PMs confused last time.

bobby: final ask: add a trace-link from a pill click into the trace explorer with prefilled filters (route, request_id, validation_error). reduces context switching.

samir: agreed. i'll own the rollout for these console changes (small PRs). andrea, can you confirm if we still see rejects after sampling bump? if yes, escalate to model-team.

andrea: will update in this thread once we have full-sample data. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
